prov.text: The provision for credit losses was $50,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as a result of net charge offs totaling $207,000, offset by an $81,000 decrease in the ACL on loans and a decrease in the reserve for unfunded commitments. The provision for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2025 was $209,000, which reflects a $172,000 increase in the ACL and net charge offs totaling $74,000, offset by a decrease in the reserve for unfunded commitments.

nonint.text: Noninterest expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 were $15.6 million and $14.0 million, respectively. Compensation and benefit expenses increased $867,000, reflecting annual merit increases, incentives, and higher medical insurance claims. Occupancy and equipment increased $156,000 and merger-related expenses were $672,000.

nonop.text: Noninterest expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 were $15.6 million and $14.0 million, respectively. Compensation and benefit expenses increased $867,000, reflecting annual merit increases, incentives, and higher medical insurance claims. Occupancy and equipment increased $156,000 and merger-related expenses were $672,000.

net.text: Net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $6.6 million, or $0.86 per diluted share, compared with $5.2 million, or $0.71 per diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $16.6 million, or $2.24 per diluted share, compared with $14.2 million, or $1.92 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income.text: Net interest income was $19.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and $16.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing 3.71% and 3.15% of interest earning assets, or NIM on a FTE basis (non-GAAP), respectively. The book yield from securities was 3.20% and 2.42% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The yield on loans increased to 5.95% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from 5.78% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in loan yields was primarily due to higher rates on new loans and variable rate commercial loans that continue to reprice. The cost of interest-bearing liabilities for the three months ended September 30, 2026 decreased to 2.08% from 2.25% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 primarily due to lower rates on money market and certificate of deposit products.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was $4.6 million and $4.3 million, respectively. Service charges and fees increased $202,000 and wealth management fees increased $94,000 due to growth in assets under management since second quarter 2025.

intro.text: Isabella Bank Corporation is a registered financial holding company registered under the BHC Act. The Corporation was incorporated in September 1988 under Michigan law. The Corporation’s wholly owned subsidiary, Isabella Bank, has 31 offices located throughout Bay, Clare, Gratiot, Isabella, Mecosta, Midland, Montcalm, and Saginaw counties. The area includes significant agricultural production, manufacturing, retail, gaming and tourism, and several colleges and universities. As used in Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations as well as in Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, references to “we,” “our,” “us,” and “the Corporation” refer to Isabella Bank Corporation, a Michigan corporation and registered financial holding company, our wholly-owned banking subsidiary, Isabella Bank, and our other consolidated subsidiaries.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
